# twenty_workspace_member

Manages access for one declared email in the provider's authenticated workspace. It does not create global users, passwords, workspaces, or sessions. Keep the operator and an independent recovery administrator outside managed resources.

The caller needs both `ROLES` and `WORKSPACE_MEMBERS`, or a full-settings grant. The role must exist in this workspace and allow assignment to users. Assigning a valid built-in, non-editable, or workspace-default role is allowed; protections against changing those role definitions do not prevent assignment.

## Example usage

```terraform
# Provider authentication is configured separately. Never manage the operator.
data "twenty_workspace" "current" {}
data "twenty_role" "member" {
  label = "Member"
}

resource "twenty_workspace_member" "declared" {
  for_each = toset(["alice@example.com", "bob@example.com"])
  email    = each.key
  role_id  = data.twenty_role.member.id
}

# workspace_id is computed and must match data.twenty_workspace.current.id.
# Existing access requires import before apply.
```

## Lifecycle

Create sends a single-email invitation with the explicit role and returns `pending`. It does not wait for login or store an invitation token/link. A fresh read changes status to `accepted` after the recipient joins, without changing the compound ID. Only `member_id`, `invitation_id`, and `expires_at` change as appropriate.

An accepted role update uses `updateWorkspaceMemberRole` with the workspace-member UUID. A pending role update revokes the validated invitation and sends a replacement. The previous mail link stops working. These are separate mutations, not a transaction.

An expired invitation reads as `expired` and plans replacement, rather than silently counting as active access. Terraform revokes the expired row and sends a fresh invitation. Create never takes over even an expired existing invitation without import. Duplicate rows for a target email, including expired rows, fail closed.

Destroy revokes pending or expired invitations, or uses `deleteUserFromWorkspace` for accepted members. The provider verifies disappearance with fresh complete reads; the returned deletion entity is the pre-deletion user-workspace row. Read failures retain state.

Changing email replaces access. Removing an email from `for_each` destroys that declared membership. Undeclared users and invitations are never evicted.

## Import

Use the lowercase workspace UUID, a slash, and the explicitly lowercase email. The workspace must match the configured provider. Member UUIDs, invitation UUIDs, labels, uppercase mailboxes, and foreign workspace IDs are rejected.

```shell
# Replace the workspace UUID and mailbox. Use the same authenticated workspace.
terraform import 'twenty_workspace_member.declared["alice@example.com"]' '77777777-7777-4777-8777-777777777777/alice@example.com'
```

Create refuses existing access. Import reads the current role without changing it. Match that role in configuration before applying; a different explicit `role_id` then plans a deliberate role change. A pending invitation with no stored role reads the current workspace default.

## Safety and recovery

Fresh identity, role assignments, members, and invitations are read under the lock shared with role resources. Operator email, user ID, workspace-member ID, and user-workspace ID are protected. Mutation guards preserve the last workspace member, a full-settings administrator, and an independent full-settings administrator outside the operator. They cannot prove recovery login reachability or identify which other resources another provider manages.

If acceptance races a pending update or revocation, the provider does not remove or reassign the newly accepted member. It returns an error. Refresh and review the next plan before retrying.

A failed send can leave a real invitation even when mail delivery or the response failed. State retains the stable ID and readable remaining access. `ownership_confirmed = false` prevents further writes until you inspect and explicitly import that access. Refresh does not silently confirm ownership. There are no automatic resends, mutation retries, rollback deletions, or multi-email sends.

Cancellation may succeed while replacement fails, leaving no access. Complete refresh then removes absent state. It may instead discover a replacement invitation requiring explicit import. See the [membership guide](../guides/membership.md) for recovery steps and server-side removal cascades.

The lock is per provider configuration, not distributed. The API has no conditional writes or transaction across these calls. Pause competing IAM writers, including other Terraform runs and provider aliases.

## Schema

### Required

- `email` (String) One bare ASCII mailbox, explicitly lowercase with no surrounding spaces. Changing it replaces access. Existing members or invitations must be imported; create never adopts them.
- `role_id` (String) Explicit lowercase UUID of a user-assignable role in this workspace. Built-in/default roles may be assigned. Accepted updates replace the member's role; pending updates revoke and reissue the invitation.

### Read-Only

- `expires_at` (String) Invitation expiration in RFC3339 format, otherwise null. Expired invitations do not count as active desired access.
- `id` (String) Stable identity and import format: lowercase workspace UUID/email. Remains unchanged when an invitation is accepted.
- `invitation_id` (String) Native invitation UUID while pending or expired, otherwise null. No invitation token or link is stored.
- `member_id` (String) Workspace-member UUID after acceptance, otherwise null. Not the global user or user-workspace ID.
- `ownership_confirmed` (Boolean) True after explicit import or a confirmed invitation send. False after an ambiguous send requires inspection and explicit import before further writes, even when refresh can see pending or accepted access. Prevents accidental adoption of a concurrent external invitation.
- `status` (String) pending, accepted, or expired on successful reads. Expired invitations plan replacement. unconfirmed or absent can remain after a failed mutation until refresh confirms the remaining access.
- `workspace_id` (String) Authenticated workspace UUID. This is not a selector.
